scope: Manually reviewed typed constructive operations, not whole-paper operational equivalence or unspecified automation.

operations: separate cycle diagnostics and memoized source errors
requirements.boundary: Checked errors and pending recursive observations are distinct. The operational semantics characterizes both completed errors and divergence; finite budget exhaustion alone is not a divergence proof.

Certified C3 is connected to actual typed object slot composition and to the safe dynamic recursive object path. Any source-style graph derivation gives exactly the same order and object observation. For finite DAGs with rank bounded by the production graph-size fuel and strictly decreasing on declared edges, complete cached/uncached batch outcomes agree for arbitrary depth and root lists, including missing-parent and inconsistent-merge errors. Validation and existing cyclic/error controls remain. The general cyclic-graph cached/reference outcome theorem is not asserted. C4 remains a separately selectable policy with its own extensions.

operations: typed ListOf and rejected mixed/improper input
recursive dynamic values and named contracts
requirements.boundary: Static typed descriptors and a recursive dynamic Value universe coexist. Dynamic contracts cover primitives, ranges, lists, dictionaries, objects, named recursive types and first-class descriptors. Current registry identity is required; budget exhaustion is an error. Lean Int/strings replace Scheme number/sexp carriers.

operations: valid-record preservation and untouched-field kernel laws
checked dynamic function boundaries with kernel soundness
dynamic schema-owned defaults, inspection, updates and wire admission
runtime descriptor factories with value-dependent parameters
requirements.boundary: Runtime descriptors expose contract constructors/arguments and open metadata in the same dynamic value universe. Functions/descriptors use explicit registry identities. Function calls check input and output refinements, with kernel admission soundness; function membership checks callability, not universal behavioral properties. Existing finite catalogs/codecs/generated updates retain their stated scope; closure serialization and unspecified universal automation are not claimed. Dynamic slot/schema catalogs now generate defaults, inspection, ordered updates and structural text/byte codecs. Catalogs describe and reconstruct themselves. Wire admission checks every nested function/descriptor identity in the current registry and returns a kernel Accepted proof. Actual lazy C3 object fields retain evaluation receipts and enter the same descriptor/wire gate. Generated codec round trips are executable controls, not a general codec inverse theorem.

Pure storage, mutable hash identities and consumed linear references share one declared slot transition. write_pureSlot and composition associativity are kernel laws. Tests compare pure/mutable/linear observations, alias visibility and persistent snapshots. Linear failure preserves the old reference; mutable failure retains prior writes. IO effect correspondence is exercised, not an unrestricted kernel IO refinement theorem. Mutable force results retain their exact immutable snapshot and kernel evaluation proof; each slot write clears memo entries and increments the generation under the same mutex.

operations: safe call-by-need cache with kernel receipts
requirements.boundary: Shared/rebuilding unsafe thunks remain executable alternatives. The safe recursive calculus supplies sound/complete finite observation, unbounded return/error semantics, divergence characterization, and least-information refinement against any fixed observation. Concrete shared-thunk parity is tested; no arbitrary unsafe-thunk equivalence is claimed. The safe shared evaluator provides proven memo receipts, cold-slot laziness, cached errors and active-path cycle diagnostics; concurrent instance reads serialize on a mutex.
